subject: Posterior of the correlation coefficient is identical to the prior

messages.author: b43184f1b55021fb
messages.subject: Posterior of the correlation coefficient is identical to the prior
parts:
I have N subjects. I obtained T1 measurements for each subject in task B and I obtained T2 measurements for each subject in task W. I suspect that there is correlation between the performance of each subject in the two tasks. Therefore I included a multivariate hierarchical prior which models the within subject correlation explicitly. The  model formulation is quite straightforward:

data {
    int<lower=0> N; // number of subjects, N=25
    int<lower=0> T1; // number of trials in task B, T1=18
    int<lower=0> T2; // number of trials in task W, T2=42
    real B[N,T1]; // measurements from task B
    real W[N,T2]; // measurements from task W
}
parameters {
    real<lower=0,upper=3> Bsd;
    real<lower=0,upper=3> Wsd;
    vector<lower=-1,upper=1>[2] mu[N];
   
    vector<lower=-1,upper=1>[2] mmu;
    vector<lower=0,upper=1>[2] msd;
    real<lower=-1,upper=1> r;
}
transformed parameters{
    matrix[2,2] S;
    S[1,1]<-square(msd[1]);
    S[2,2]<-square(msd[2]);
    S[2,1]<-msd[1]*msd[2]*r;
    S[1,2]<-S[2,1];
}
model {
    for (n in 1:N){
        mu[n] ~ multi_normal(mmu,S);
        for (t in 1:T1) B[n,t] ~ normal(mu[n,1],Bsd);
        for (t in 1:T2) W[n,t]~ normal(mu[n,2],Wsd);
    }
}


When I fit this model I get posterior estimates of r that are identical to its prior i.e. mean is around 0 and 95% interval goes from -0.9 to 0.9. Posterior estimates of the other parameters are very similar to the estimates from a model without the correlation coefficient that is where S[2,1]=S[1,2]=0.

Does this mean that the data provide no information about the correlation? This seems very odd to me. I suspect I'm doing something wrong. Maybe someone can spot the problem.

Thanks in advance for any suggestions,

Matus

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Posterior of the correlation coefficient is identical to the prior
parts:
I'd start with a scatterplot of the n means by subject,
mean(B[n,]) by mean(W[n,]), to see what the correlation actually
looks like.

Are your constraints on the means and standard deviations all
reasonable?

Has the model converged when you fit it? Can you simulate
fake data with correlation from the model and fit it with the model?

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Posterior of the correlation coefficient is identical to the prior
parts:
Hi Bob,

I previously looked at the correlations between the posterior estimates of mmu (=the subject mean) in a model without corr coef and with and without hierachical prior (partial pooling/no pooling). I get correlation around 0.2-0.3. Now I also did compute the correlations between the raw means as you suggested which gives r ~ 0.05. The scatterplots look ok. No extreme values or outliers. Approx normal, though it's just 25 values.

Actually it is fairly plausible that there is no correlation, I would just expect that the CI somewhat shrinks. E.g. using Fisher transformation for N=25 the 95% CI around 0 is [-0.4, 0.4]. This is what bothers me.

The parameter constraints are ok and the model converges well (all Rhat<1.05) and fairly quickly.

I should also mention that the values of W are logit transformed from range [0,1] to -inf,inf (logit-normal model). This should not be a problem. All subject means are in the range [0.45,0.55] where logit is approx. linear.

I will try fake data simulation next, that's always a good idea.

m.
